page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-4GB is an entry-level instance configured for budget-conscious and burstable utility workloads. It is virtualized on a KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a single shared vCPU derived from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Bundled with the instance is 30 GB of local SSD storage, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU flag profile features AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), and cryptographic hardware acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded instruction performance balanced against strict single-core resource limitations. In single-threaded compression benchmarks, the AMD core achieves top-tier results, reaching 38.56 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.51 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 2108.0. Conversely, all multi-threaded operations reflect the constraints of a single shared execution core; the Geekbench multi-core score registers at 2182.0, while PassMark CPU and database operation metrics fall into lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth performance is mixed, demonstrating average write throughput of 31.28 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, but lower read performance at 36.02 GB/sec.

Given the shared single-core setup, the server provides economical entry-tier computing where consistent parallel processing is not required. It is not architected for continuous multi-core execution, intensive ray tracing, heavy database hosting, or large model inference. Appropriate workload fits include low-traffic web serving, development and staging servers, single-threaded text processing pipelines, lightweight batch utilities, and microservices.
